user.title: LumaPresence
user.description: Name this instance and choose the lights the simulation may control.

facades.title: Facades
facades.description: Mark the simulation lights visible from the street (front) or from the back of the house (rear). The rest count as interior lights.

data_description.front_lights: Visible from the street. A minimum of them is kept on while simulating.
data_description.rear_lights: Visible from the back of the house. A minimum of them is kept on while simulating.

learning.title: Learning
learning.description: Choose where LumaPresence learns how the house is really used. Every light in these floors and areas is learned, except disabled and hidden entities and configuration or diagnostic entities such as status LEDs. Simulation lights are always learned.

data_description.learn_floors: Lights in every area of these floors are learned.
data_description.learn_areas: Indoor areas that do not belong to any of the floors above.
data_description.learn_extra: For example relays exposed as switches, or lamps without an area.
data_description.learn_auto_exclude_indicators: Leave out a light whose device also has a main switch: smart plugs and relays often expose their status LED as a light. Setting switches (disabled, configuration or diagnostic) do not count, and lights with color or color temperature are never left out. Add a lamp that is wrongly left out to the extra entities.
data_description.learn_only_human: Ignore light changes made by automations and scripts.

monitoring.title: Monitoring
monitoring.description: Raise a Repairs issue, and fire the `luma_presence_light_unavailable` event, when a simulation or route light stays unavailable.

data.unavailable_alert_minutes: Alert if a light is unavailable for (minutes)
data.verify_timeout: Wait for a light to obey (seconds)

data_description.report_notify: A notify entity (notify.my_phone) or service (notify.mobile_app_my_phone). Leave it empty to only fire the luma_presence_night_report event.
data_description.verify_timeout: After each command LumaPresence checks that the light reached the expected state, retries once, and otherwise uses another light of the same room. 0 turns the check off.

dream.title: Dream
dream.description: Dream generates new nights from what LumaPresence has learned about your house. Each night it creates several candidates and keeps the most realistic one that is not too similar to the last nights.

data_description.dream_candidates: Nights generated before choosing the most realistic one.
data_description.dream_max_similarity: A candidate more similar than this to one of the last 7 nights (share of the same rooms at the same times) is discarded.

context.title: Context
context.description: Optional context for the simulation: start the evening when it gets dark, wake the house up before dawn, use workdays and holidays for the type of each night and morning, and add light when the weather is bad. With an illuminance sensor, a daylight guard also stops everything and switches the lights off as soon as it is day.

data.morning_enabled: Wake-up in Sun and Time modes
data.morning_learned_enabled: Wake-up in Replay and Dream modes

data_description.darkness_sensor: The evening starts when it has stayed below the threshold for 5 minutes, between the earliest and the latest start. Without readings, at sunset.
data_description.darkness_threshold_lx: Below this illuminance it counts as dark.
data_description.darkness_latest_min: If it is not dark by then, the evening starts anyway.
data_description.morning_enabled: Sun and Time: lights on from the wake-up start until it is light.
data_description.morning_learned_enabled: Replay and Dream: from the time the house usually wakes up (learned), never before the wake-up start, until it is light.
data_description.morning_start: Earliest wake-up. If the simulation is switched on during the wake-up, it starts a few minutes later.
data_description.morning_nonworkday_mode: Sun and Time only (Replay and Dream follow what they learned). Later: start at the non-workday wake-up time. Do not simulate: no wake-up on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays.
data_description.morning_nonworkday_start: Used with Later. Must be later than the wake-up start. If it is already light by then, there is no wake-up that day.
data_description.morning_latest_min: With an illuminance sensor, the wake-up ends when it has been light for 5 minutes; if it is still dark, up to this long after sunrise. Without a sensor it ends at sunrise.
data_description.workday_sensor: A Workday integration sensor: decides which days are workdays (preferred over the holiday calendar).
data_description.holiday_calendar: All-day events (or events covering midday) are holidays: the night before one is a weekend night. Do not use the Workday calendar here (its events are workdays): use the Workday sensor instead.
data_description.weather_entity: Rain, snow, storms, hail or less than 8 °C count as bad weather.
data_description.bad_weather_boost: Dream: the two busiest evening rooms start this much more often. Sun and Time: one more light on.

covers.title: Covers
covers.description: Blinds, shutters and curtains open in the morning and close at dusk, only during a real absence (alarm armed away or vacation, or nobody home), never during a test. Awnings, garage doors, gates and doors are never used: awnings can be damaged by wind, and doors, garages and gates are a security risk. Covers are not blocked by the daylight guard.

data.covers_close_delay_min: Close up to this long after dark (minutes)

data_description.covers: Blinds, shutters, curtains, shades and windows. Awnings, garage doors, gates and doors are not offered.
data_description.covers_mode: Schedule: the times below. Learned: the times your household opens and closes each cover (Replay plays its source night, otherwise they are sampled per day type); the schedule is used while a cover has fewer than 7 observed days.
data_description.covers_open_position: Position used to open covers that support it (100 = fully open).
data_description.covers_open_nonworkday: Saturdays, Sundays and holidays (Workday sensor or holiday calendar from the Context section). Never before sunrise.
data_description.covers_close_delay_min: Covers close when the evening gets dark (the darkness decision of the Context section, or sunset), each one after a random delay up to this long.

ambience.title: Ambience
ambience.description: Optional sound: a media player plays while its room is occupied in tonight's simulation, only during a real absence, never after the quiet time and never while it is day. The previous volume and source are restored afterwards. The TV backlight (WLED or similar) needs nothing here: add it as a simulation light.

data_description.ambience_players: Each player must be in an area: it plays while a simulation light of that area is on.
data_description.ambience_media: One line per player, `media_player.living_room = MEDIA_ID` (for example a radio stream). A line without a player is used for every player without a line of its own.
data_description.ambience_quiet_after: No sound from this time until noon.

deterrence.title: Deterrence
deterrence.description: When a trigger outside detects someone at night during a real absence, the house reacts like people waking up: a light of that facade, then the lights toward the door, for a few minutes. Lights only: never sirens, locks or doors. Add triggers from the integration page (Add deterrence trigger).

data_description.deterrence_enabled: Off by default. Active while it is dark: from the evening darkness decision (or sunset) until it is day, whether or not the simulation window is running.
data_description.deterrence_cooldown_min: A trigger does not react again until this long after its last reaction.
data_description.deterrence_max_per_night: Further detections are ignored until the next night.

ai.title: AI (optional)
ai.description: Optional generative AI through an AI task entity (for example a cloud or local model you have set up). It can add a scenario to some Dream evenings and write the morning report. What is sent, and nothing else: the night type, month and season, sunset rounded to 15 minutes, bad-weather and holiday flags, and for each room an opaque key (room_1, room_2...) with a generic type (bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, living, office, hall, other), its expected occupancy per hour, typical hours and typical visit length; for the report, last night's simulation with the same keys. Never sent: entity IDs, room or area names, people, learned events, dates of real days, location, alarm states or cameras. Room names are put back locally. Leave the entity empty to turn everything off.

data.ai_report: Write the morning report with AI
data.ai_max_calls_per_day: AI calls per day at most

data_description.ai_scenario_probability: Share of Dream evenings that get a scenario (guests for dinner, movie night...). The wake-up is never changed.
data_description.ai_report: The notification text is written by the AI; the event keeps its data. If the AI fails, the usual text is sent.
data_description.ai_max_calls_per_day: When the limit is reached, AI features are skipped until the next day.

user.title: Route
user.description: A path someone walks at night: from the origin (for example the bedroom), along the path lights in order, to the destination (for example the bathroom), and back. Route lights do not need to be simulation lights.

data_description.origin: Light turned on first, for example the bedroom light.
data_description.path: Lights in between, in walking order, for example the hallway.
data_description.destination: Light where the walk ends, for example the bathroom light.
